headline: All majors above the 200-day line with overbought momentum, but whales are moving coins onto exchanges at the fastest weekly pace in a month.
paragraphs: The regime is unified and elevated. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, and ADA are all trading above their 200-day simple moving averages, establishing a broad uptrend across the majors. None of the assets show a golden cross, meaning the 50-day has not yet reclaimed the 200-day on any of them, but the fact that prices sit comfortably above the longer-term anchor is the primary structural signal. Only Dogecoin sits below its 200-day line, a notable exception among the top holdings. The week-long and month-long moves tell the story of momentum: Bitcoin has climbed 24.7% over seven days and 24.3% over 30 days; Solana has gained 40.5% on the week; XRP has run 45.3%. This is not a correction or a sideways hold. This is an advance.

Against that backdrop, momentum indicators are flashing overbought conditions across nearly every major. Bitcoin RSI-14 sits at 82.3, Solana at 85.2, Ethereum at 77.9, and BNB at 81.3. All of these are well into the 70+ zone where momentum typically begins to rest or reverse. MACD remains above its signal line for all seven assets shown, confirming the uptrend is intact, but overbought RSI without a golden cross is a configuration that often precedes a correction or a consolidation, not a continuation. The tension here is real: the trend is up and accelerating in price, but the meter says the move has run far and fast. Dogecoin, trading below its 200-day despite an RSI of 67.9 and positive MACD, is the clearest divergence: momentum is firm but the asset has not yet reclaimed its longer-term footing.

Funding across the major perpetual contracts is modestly bullish but not extreme. Bitcoin funding sits at 0.05% per 8 hours, or 0.5% annualized, and Bitcoin open interest stands at 2.26 billion USD with a 1.02 long-to-short ratio, suggesting roughly balanced positioning with a slight long lean. Ethereum funding is higher at 0.19% per 8 hours (2.1% annualized), and ETH open interest is 1.56 billion USD with a 1.23 ratio, more bullish. Both are positive, meaning longs are paying to hold the bet, but neither rate is punitive. Solana shows a negative funding rate of negative 0.11% per 8 hours (negative 1.2% annualized), a signal that shorts are paying, yet open interest is 368 million USD with a 1.12 ratio. Dogecoin funding has turned sharply negative at negative 0.31% per 8 hours (negative 3.4% annualized), the sharpest divergence on the board: longs are heavily overbought relative to shorts, and the funding structure is now paying shorts to hold. Liquidations over the past 16 to 24 hours have been asymmetric across assets: on Bitcoin and Solana, shorts are being wiped out far more than longs, but on Ethereum the count leans similarly ($15.8M in short liquidations versus $8.4M in long), and on Dogecoin the pattern mirrors Ethereum. When funding is negative and shorts are still being liquidated more than longs, it suggests the crowd of leveraged shorts is crowded and underwater.

Whale flows reveal the critical tension of the day. Over the past 48 hours, 169.9 million USD in net value moved onto exchanges, the largest recent inflow. The week ending August 27 saw 1.056 billion USD move onto exchanges, the heaviest weekly net inflow in the digest. The two preceding weeks (Aug 20 and Aug 13) also saw inflows of 383 million and 898 million respectively. Three weeks of sustained inflows onto exchanges, accelerating into this week, is a supply signal: large holders are positioning coins to sell or to be ready to sell. Bitcoin has seen a small net outflow of 369 thousand USD off exchanges over 48 hours, but that masks the underlying churn: 181 million came in while 181.6 million went out, nearly a wash. Ethereum, by contrast, saw 170 million move onto exchanges with zero outflow, a unidirectional move. The biggest single whale moves over 48 hours landed at Coinbase and Coinbase Institutional: 68 million in Bitcoin, 67 million in Ethereum, and 59 million in more Bitcoin, all landing on the exchange or its institutional arm. Simultaneously, 62 million in Bitcoin moved off Binance and 59 million off Coinbase, suggesting a rotate or a staged exit. The stablecoin float sits at 309 billion USD, up 0.76% over 30 days, a modest increase that has not kept pace with the price rally.

The Fear & Greed index stands at 71, labeled Greed, near the top of its 30-day range of 25 to 74. Spot ETF flows remain positive: Bitcoin saw 232 million in net inflow on August 26, and Ethereum saw 192 million, with eight consecutive days of inflows for each. Bitcoin has accumulated 54.7 billion USD cumulatively in flows, Ethereum 12.6 billion. This traditional-finance bid is real and persistent. Yet the whale flows onto exchanges and the extreme RSI readings create a contradiction: the crowd is greedy and the ETF machine is buying, but the largest wallets are moving coins to where they can be sold. This disagreement, between retail and institutional inflows via spot products and the big players repositioning for liquidity, is the structural risk in the tape.

What to watch: whether funding remains positive as RSI retreats from overbought levels, and whether the weekly whale inflow onto exchanges reverses or continues. A flip in Bitcoin funding to negative while price holds above the 200-day would be a clear signal of longs losing conviction. A sustained pattern of inflows onto exchanges over another week, combined with a move below 65 on RSI, would suggest the big players are ahead of a pullback. Conversely, if whale flows rotate back off exchanges and funding remains paid while RSI remains elevated, the structure would be confirming the uptrend despite the overbought meter. The Dogecoin divergence (below the 200-day, negative funding, overbought RSI) is worth tracking separately; it may foreshadow a broader rotation away from the more speculative names.
